title: Lock the alias full-width contract across the whole render path
goal: PROBLEM: The alias screen was squeezed by a width cap (max-w-2xl, then a plan-guessed max-w-4xl = 896px on a 1440px page) while the issue explicitly complained the rest of the page sat empty. Both the implementation agent and the PR-review agent accepted the still-capped version; only a human rejection ("make the most of the full width") forced a full rework loop (design-note update, uncapped w-full min-w-0 section root, new desktop+mobile screenshots, test updates, re-review). The width target was a guessed Tailwind step, never a measurable criterion derived from the complaint. The current regression test (frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsCards.overflow.test.jsx, "spans the full width") locks only the section root and row classes, not the ancestor chain: App.jsx main -> settings section -> tabpanel -> ProjectSettingsForm wrapper -> alias section. A cap reintroduced on any ancestor (e.g. the max-w-2xl in ProjectSettings.jsx:259, today confined to the project-tab conditional) would re-squeeze the Aliases tab with no test failing. FIX: (1) Extend the overflow contract test to render the settings page on the Aliases tab and assert no max-w-* class (other than max-w-full/max-w-none) on the alias section or any ancestor between the settings panel and the section, so refactors cannot silently reintroduce a cap. (2) Add a one-paragraph rule where Plan agents will see it (frontend agent/UI guidance): when an issue complains about wasted space or truncation, the plan must state a measurable width criterion (uncapped w-full min-w-0 with no max-w on the render path; zero clipped elements at the stated viewports) instead of guessing a Tailwind max-w step, and must verify it headlessly. Case study with full history: task 158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972 (docs/tasks/158394ab-3b43-4813-b94a-32d772a79972/: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Step 2, DESIGN-NOTE.md section (d), review-alias-redo-20261120.md, review-fullwidth-20261120.md, final-review-20261120-211044.md).
